# Terelj Wellness Resort — AI & LLM Overview

## What is Terelj Wellness Resort?

Terelj Wellness Resort is a planned villa-led mountain wellness retreat in Gorkhi-Terelj National Park, Töv Province, Mongolia. It comprises 47 private wellness villas and 8 glamping pods on 5 hectares, built in three phases over five years. The site is 50–76 km, about 1.5–2 hours by road, north-east of Ulaanbaatar.

All images on the website are design-stage visualisations and may change through detailed design.

## Project Summary

- **Name:** Terelj Wellness Resort (テレルジ・ウェルネスリゾート / 特勒吉康养度假村)
- **Location:** Gorkhi-Terelj National Park, Töv Province, Mongolia (47.879850°N, 107.405738°E)
- **Site area:** 5 hectares, about 90% kept as natural grassland
- **Distance from Ulaanbaatar:** 50–76 km, about 1.5–2 hours by road
- **Accommodation:** 47 private wellness villas + 8 glamping pods
- **Project type:** Villa-led wellness resort, built in three phases
- **Investment stage:** Open to investment partners; investment deck available on request
- **Guest markets:** Ulaanbaatar residents, China, South Korea, Japan, United States, Europe, Australia

## Phasing

1. **Phase 1 (Year 1, 1.5 ha) — 15 villas:** wellness villas with private sauna, deep bath and full-height mountain glazing; lobby; reformer room; 80-seat restaurant with juice and herbal tea bar; open-air platform for sunrise classes. Soft opening about six months after construction starts.
2. **Phase 2 (Years 2–3, +1.5 ha) — 20 more villas:** herbal-steam villas with cold plunge pools, screen-free villas, a 200 sqm traditional therapy centre with heated pool, an organic greenhouse.
3. **Phase 3 (Years 4–5, +2 ha) — 12 more villas and 8 glamping pods:** hot-spring villas, which depend on a planned geothermal well (a survey comes before drilling; heated mineral-water pools are the fallback); conservation zone with WWF Mongolia; solar-powered glamping pods.

**Later option, decided separately:** a main building with about 40 hotel rooms and an event hall, built only once villa demand is proven. It is not part of the current plan.

## Wellness Programme

Services open with the phase that builds their facility (P1–P3).

- **Movement:** pilates and yoga, including sunrise sessions (P1); guided forest and ridge walks (P1); breathwork (P1)
- **Heat, cold and water:** private sauna in every villa (P1); winter snow-and-sauna ritual (P1); Mongolian herbal steam with cold plunge (P2); heated indoor pool (P2); private hot-spring villas from a planned geothermal well (P3)
- **Traditional Mongolian therapies:** in-villa herbal oil massage (P1); consultation with a traditional practitioner (P2); bone-setting by a bariachi (P2); moxibustion and cupping (P2); herbal and mineral baths (P2)
- **Food:** cold-pressed juice and herbal tea bar (P1); summer airag with a herder family (P1); 3, 5 and 7-day detox menus (P2); cooking classes (P2)
- **Mind and rest:** screen-free villas and sleep programme (P1); morin khuur sound sessions (P1); stargazing (P1); guided meditation and silent retreats (P2)
- **Nature, culture and groups:** herder family visits and riding (P1); corporate retreats and buyouts (P1); grassland restoration with WWF Mongolia (P3); small weddings and festivals (P3)

Traditional therapies are offered as wellness services by qualified practitioners, not as medical treatment.

### Signature Programmes (inclusive packages)

| Programme | Length | For |
|-----------|--------|-----|
| City Reset | 2–3 nights | Ulaanbaatar residents, weekends |
| Steppe Detox | 5 nights | Guests from Korea, Japan and China, summer |
| Winter Sauna Retreat | 7 nights | Long-haul and corporate guests, December–February |

## Year-Round Calendar

- **Summer:** sunrise pilates on the open-air platform, walks in the park, meals on the terrace.
- **Winter (December–February):** sauna and herbal therapy retreats. Glazed galleries link every building.

## Market (with sources)

- Mongolia had a record **847,170 foreign visitors in 2025**, up **16.5%** on 2024. (National Statistics Office of Mongolia, via CEIC)
- Tourism revenue in 2025: **$1.6B**. (Ministry of Environment and Tourism, via GoGo Mongolia)
- Government target: **2 million foreign visitors a year by 2030**. (The UB Post, Feb 2025)
- Arrivals in the first half of 2026 were up 19.8% on 2025; the full-year 2025 total was passed by early October. (Asia News Network, Jul 2026; Travel and Tour World, Oct 2026)
- 47% of visitors come for eco and adventure experiences. (The UB Post, Feb 2025)
- 3.2M domestic trips in 2024. (NSO Domestic Tourism Survey 2025, via GoGo Mongolia)
- Global wellness tourism grew **11.4%** in 2024–25 and **15.6%** in Asia; thermal and mineral springs grew **10.4%**; the global wellness economy reached **$7.5T** in 2025. (Global Wellness Institute, Global Wellness Economy Monitor 2026)
- Gorkhi-Terelj is Mongolia's most visited national park. Its accommodation is mostly camps and mid-range resorts, with one established luxury hotel.

## Guest Markets and Access

- **China:** direct flights from Beijing, Shanghai, Hohhot, Ordos and Hong Kong
- **South Korea:** about 3 h 40 from Seoul, around 35 direct flights a week; 90 days visa-free
- **Japan:** direct from Tokyo and Osaka, about 40 flights a week from Tokyo
- **United States:** one stop via Seoul, Tokyo, Beijing or Istanbul
- **Europe:** direct from Frankfurt and Istanbul; EU visa-free through 2026
- **Australia:** one stop via Seoul, Hong Kong or Beijing; 30 days visa-free
